newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Pertamina restarts Balongan refinery.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Pertamina restarts Balongan refinery.

text.p: Indonesian state oil company Pertamina restarted the crude distilllation unit (CDU) at the Balongan refinery at 75 percent of capacity on Saturday, company sources said on Monday.
They said the refinery's residue catalytic cracker (RCC) unit was restarted on Sunday.
"We resumed the CDU operations on Saturday at 75 percent capacity. We have also restarted the RCC on Sunday with 80 percent capacity," one source said.
"Everything is working fine. There is no problem. We will gradually increase the capacity in the coming days," the source said.
Pertamina's Balongan refinery is located in West Java and has a capacity of 125,000 barrels per day (bpd).
The company sources said the atmospheric residue hydrodesulphuriser was also restarted on Saturday.
The RCC, which has a capacity of 83,000 bpd, has been shut since February because of technical problems.
The CDU has been open only sporadically since the RCC was closed down.
